Package net.raphimc.viabedrock.api.chunk.light

Class LightEngine

java.lang.Object
net.raphimc.viabedrock.api.chunk.light.LightEngine
public final class LightEngine extends Object
Computes Minecraft style sky and block light for a chunk using the block data of the chunk and its eight neighbors. The propagation algorithm is a breadth first flood fill, based on the light engine of Minestom (https://github.com/Minestom/Minestom, Apache License 2.0).

Light behaves like on the Java Edition client: light entering a block loses a level of max(1, opacity) of that block. Sky light of level 15 travels downwards without losing level as long as it does not enter a light filtering block. Blocks with an opacity of 15 or above fully block light.

  • Method Details

    • computeRegionLight

      public static ChunkLight[] computeRegionLight(int[][][] regionStates, int sectionCount, boolean skyLight, byte[] emissionTable, byte[] opacityTable)
      Computes the light of all chunks of a 3x3 chunk region. The lighting needs of every chunk in the region are fully covered by the region, as light travels at most 15 blocks.
      Parameters:
      regionStates - The java block states of the region, indexed as [chunkIndex][sectionIndex][blockIndex] where chunkIndex = (chunkZOffset + 1) * 3 + (chunkXOffset + 1) and blockIndex = y * 256 | z * 16 | x. Chunks and sections that have not been loaded are null and are treated as fully opaque.
      sectionCount - The amount of chunk sections of a chunk column
      skyLight - Whether the dimension has sky light
      emissionTable - Light emission (0-15) per java block state id
      opacityTable - Light opacity (0-15) per java block state id
      Returns:
      The light data of all loaded chunks of the region; null for unloaded chunks

    • brightenBlockLight

      public static ChunkLight[] brightenBlockLight(int[][][] regionStates, int sectionCount, int sourceX, int sourceY, int sourceZ, int emission, byte[] opacityTable, ChunkLight[] previousLights)
      Adds the light contributed by a newly brighter block in the center chunk. The cached light must represent the region before this one emission increase; opacity must be unchanged. Other edits, including removing a light source, require a full recomputation.
